NoteNlpAccessor::remove_boilerplate¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteNlpAccessor::remove_boilerplate() const

Delete Recognizable Policy And Rights Lines¶

remove_boilerplate() removes complete lines that look like recurring rights, policy, terms, or disclaimer material. It exists for document bodies whose useful prose has been mixed with site or publication furniture. The method is intentionally a small deterministic filter, not a classifier: it removes only the line forms in the table below.

Recognition rule

Examples that match

Trimmed line starts with the complete word copyright

Copyright 2026 Pluss

Trimmed line starts with ©

© 2026 Pluss

Line contains all rights reserved

Pluss, all rights reserved.

Line contains privacy policy

Read our Privacy Policy

Line contains terms of service

Terms of Service apply

Trimmed line starts with the complete word disclaimer

Disclaimer: preliminary

Matching is ASCII case-insensitive. The copyright and disclaimer boundary rules matter: copyrighted study and disclaimer_value are not treated as the standalone trigger words. Likewise, isolated words such as privacy, terms, or rights do not match. This narrow vocabulary makes the operation predictable, but it cannot discover paraphrased notices or decide whether a matching policy sentence is substantively important. Do not use it where such lines must be retained as evidence.

When at least one line matches, all matching lines are deleted and the remaining ASCII whitespace is collapsed to single spaces, with edge whitespace stripped. This turns a surviving multiline document into one compact cell. If no line matches, the original cell is returned byte-for-byte, including line breaks and edge spaces. A cell made entirely from recognized lines becomes the empty string; the cell is not removed from the Note.

The receiver is unchanged. The result is a fresh Text Note with identical rank, extents, and cell order. Empty Text Notes remain empty, undefined propagates, and Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes reject. Static trigger prechecks avoid line processing for cells that contain none of the relevant vocabulary.

Example 1: Remove Several Recognized Line Forms¶

const auto source = pluss::note::make({
    "Project note\nCopyright 2026 Pluss\nPrivacy Policy\n"
    "This copyrighted study remains.\nTerms of service apply\n"
    "Disclaimer: draft\nAll rights reserved",
});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    source.nlp().remove_boilerplate()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Project note This copyrighted study remains."]

The ordinary sentence survives because copyrighted is not the complete trigger word at the beginning of its trimmed line.

Example 2: A No-Match Cell Is Exactly Preserved¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({
        " Privacy engineering\nand contractual terms remain unchanged. "})
        .nlp().remove_boilerplate()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
[" Privacy engineering\nand contractual terms remain unchanged. "]

Neither the newline nor edge spaces are normalized because no line was removed.

Example 3: Removing A Whole Cell Does Not Change Shape¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"Copyright 2026", "a (draft)",
                             "- item", "use `x` now"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    matrix.nlp().remove_boilerplate()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["", "a (draft)"], 
  ["- item", "use `x` now"]
]

Example 4: Idempotence¶

const auto once = source.nlp().remove_boilerplate();
std::cout << "boilerplate idempotent=" << std::boolalpha
          << (once.nlp().remove_boilerplate() == once).all().bool_item()
          << '\n';

Output¶

boilerplate idempotent=true
